units.title: Fog, as promised
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Morning. The fog has arrived on schedule, which is more than can be said for most things. A few points:
- The supply skipper will still run, but slowly, and he may hold at Gilliver if he can't see the landing.
- If an order matters this week, place it early in the day.
- Please note visibility in the remarks line of the day report so head office understand any slow days.
Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Spare chains and bars
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi. The store has asked me to pass on that they're holding spare chains, bars and files for the Holm job on the shelf by the loading door, so if anything wears faster than expected in the wet, add it to your order and it'll go on the next boat. They'd rather send too many than have saws idle. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Small correction to this morning's note: the store is out of the longer bars until the wholesaler's van comes, which they think will be early next week. Chains and files are fine. Apologies, I should have checked before sending. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Courier piece on the boats
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: The Courier has run a piece about the supply boats at Gilliver. It's harmless: the boats, the fuel berth, a lady sad about her view. Our line was that it's a large but routine clearance, which it is. If anyone at the landing or on the boat asks you questions for a paper, please point them to me rather than answering. Nothing sinister, it just keeps things tidy. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Generator hours
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi. Fleet maintenance would like a reading from the generator hours counter when you next do the day report. The service interval is 250 hours and they want to schedule a filter change before the camp gets near it. Filters and the sheet are in the grey box in the camper, I'm told. If you can't find the box, say so and I'll chase them. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: First aid kit check (monthly)
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Monthly reminder from H&S: please check the first aid kit against the list inside the lid and note anything used or out of date. The eyewash bottles in particular tend to go cloudy in cold weather. Replacements can go on the supply order. You don't need to send me the list, just tick the box on the day report. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Day four
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: End of day four from the office. Head office are content, which in my experience is the most they ever are. The Met Office has the fog staying for several days, so please plan for slow mornings. Keep everyone close to camp after dark and don't let anyone wander off to look at the fog, however pretty it is from the shore. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: is it foggy where you are because it is here
units.author: sam
units.text: hi! Sound FM has been doing a fog live page all day, and I followed it at work instead of shelving, which tells you how exciting Tollinby is. they said Carrow Point has its foghorn going and the neighbours are livid. anyway. Jamie had rehearsal tonight and has decided Second Reed should have a limp. nobody asked for a limp. the director allowed it. love, S x

units.author: sam
units.text: forgot to say, Mum's hospital letter came. it's a date to see the consultant about the hip, not the operation yet, and she says it's 'a fuss about nothing' while holding onto the kitchen counter. I'll take her. she said to say she's proud of you and to wear a hat. she says that every time, so consider yourself told. love, S x

units.title: Which month do trees hate? (Sep-timber.)
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Chief. I know it's not September. I don't care. Road job update: we cut a bank back today and found a shopping trolley, a fridge door and a sign for a pub that closed before I was born. The client wants the sign. The client can't have the sign. It's going on my shed. How's island life? Are you sleeping in the camper or have you gone full hermit in a hollow log?

units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: One serious one, then I'll go back to being delightful. Fog on a clearance makes people careless in the afternoon, when they've stopped noticing it. Morning everybody's careful. Two o'clock is when somebody walks into a lane without shouting. Make them shout. That's it. Back to the pub sign.

units.title: The fog on the news
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Hi, I'm so sorry to write again. The Evening Post says the fog is coming all the way up to the port here, so I imagine it's worse where you are. Could you tell Tomas I'm fine and not to worry about the car, it's booked in? And if you notice, is he sleeping? He never sleeps well somewhere new. You don't have to answer. Thank you, Ana

units.title: Lantern Week starts NOW! Light up the long evenings
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: It's Lantern Week at Camp Supply! The evenings are drawing in, and nothing says cosy like a warm pool of light outside your tent or cabin. Our Beacon range is the brightest in the Sound, with a 40-hour runtime on one set of batteries. Order before Sunday for free delivery to any mainland address!

units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Camp tip of the week! Hang your lantern at head height, not on the ground: it lights more of the space around you and keeps the glare out of your eyes. Two lanterns at opposite corners mean no dark corners at all. Happy camping from all of us at Camp Supply!

units.title: Still foggy
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Morning. Second day of fog. No pressure from me, but head office will ask at Friday's meeting, so I'm just checking where we are on numbers. The day report is fine; I don't need anything extra. If the fog has slowed things down, say so plainly and I'll explain it upstairs. That's what I'm for. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Felling in poor visibility
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
A slightly formal one, sorry. H&S have asked every site to confirm the poor-visibility rule:
- No felling unless the whole drop zone and the escape route are visible.
- Two tree lengths between workers, always.
- Shout before you cut, every time.
If that means fewer trees on a foggy day, that's the right answer. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Wages showing outstanding
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi. Payroll's report this morning still shows crew wages outstanding on the site account. I don't want to nag, and I know the fog isn't helping the money come in. But on an island people notice quickly when they haven't been paid, and the contract lets anyone left unpaid past their due day walk off the job. Oldest first, please. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Planning around the gap
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi. Following the leaver notice: I've asked whether we can find a replacement, and the answer is still no, not mid-contract and not out there. I'm sorry. Please plan the lanes around who you have, and don't let anyone take on two people's work to make up the numbers. Tired crews make bad decisions in fog. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Gilliver slip
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: For information only. The supply skipper tells me the night ferry crew reported someone trespassing at the end of the Gilliver slipway late last night, in the fog. It's nothing to do with us, but the harbour office are asking boat users to keep the slip clear, so our boat may load at the fuel berth for a few days. It shouldn't affect timings. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Timesheets for week one
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi. Week one timesheets close at the end of day seven. Your day reports cover most of it, but Payroll would like the rest days and any half days recorded properly, so nobody is short when the statement goes out. If someone worked a half day in the fog, please write it as a half, not a full. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Site evacuation plan
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi. After the trade journal mentioned remote sites needing an evacuation plan, a director asked whether ours is current. It is. It's the blue folder in the camper desk drawer: boat, radio channel, muster point at the landing, my number and the coastguard's. Could you read it once this week so you know where it is? I'd rather you never need it. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Day five
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: End of day five. Thank you for the report. The office is quiet; half of Port Ammet seems to have stayed at home in the fog, and the other half is in the canteen complaining about it. The forecast is no better tomorrow. Please keep fires sensible and everyone in at a decent hour. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Statement: contract days 4 to 5 (ref GLS-KH-0001-D05)
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Interim statement. Reference: GLS-KH-0001-D05. Covering: contract days 4 and 5. Day rate applied: $300.00 per active employee-day, as per contract schedule B. All amounts for this interval are posted to the wages page of your Journal. The full period 1 statement will be issued after day 7 closes. Queries go to your operations manager, not to this mailbox, which is not monitored.

units.title: Reminder: liabilities past due (ref GLS-KH-0001-A02)
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Reminder. Reference: GLS-KH-0001-A02. Status: unpaid employee-day liabilities remain on this site account. Settle the oldest due first. Liabilities unpaid after their due day closes may result in an employee leaving the contract. This reminder is generated each statement day while a balance remains. This is an automated message. Please do not reply to this address.

units.title: Roster change recorded (ref GLS-KH-0001-L02)
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Roster notice. Reference: GLS-KH-0001-L02. Status: the site roster reflects one or more closed employee records. Closed records accrue no day rate. Any final liabilities remain payable and appear on the wages page of your Journal until settled. This is an automated message. Please do not reply to this address.

units.title: the glove situation is resolved
units.author: sam
units.text: you'll be relieved to hear the dog has, ahem, returned the glove. the vet said it would pass and it did and that is all I am saying in writing. he's very pleased with himself and has been eyeing the oven glove since. I've put everything woolly on the top shelf like we're childproofing for a goat. anyway how are you? love, S x

units.title: they're cutting our hours
units.author: sam
units.text: so it was on Sound FM today, the council is closing Tollinby library an hour earlier from next week. that last hour is when the sixth formers come in and the man from the night shift at the depot who reads every sea novel we have. they quoted 'a part-time assistant'. that was me!! I said it before I knew it was going on air. anyway, there's a petition. love, S x

units.author: sam
units.text: update, the petition is at 300 and my manager has 'had a word', meaning she bought me a coffee and said well done and also please don't talk to the radio again without telling her. Mum has signed it twice, once as herself and once as 'a concerned reader'. I have not told her that's not how it works. love, S x

units.title: Why was the lumberjack sacked? (He kept axing questions.)
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Chief. The fog's got as far inland as the road job, so today we stood in a lay-by for three hours watching the foreman read the paper. Paid, mind. Saw the bit in the Courier about the Holm boats. Ruth's line was 'large but routine'. That's Ruth, that is. She'd call a volcano 'a warm site with some challenges'. Decent, though. For management.

units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Also, since you'll be in the camper with the fog round you: get a pack of cards and a proper board game in on the boat. Not the phone. Phones are fine until the signal goes, and then everyone sits there staring at nothing. Last camp I ran, we had a cribbage league. I lost. I'm still bitter.

units.title: Is Tomas all right?
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Hi, I'm sorry, this is probably silly. A friend who works at the ferry terminal said she'd heard someone came back from the island early this week. I'm sure he would have rung me if it were him, but his phone barely works out there and I keep thinking about it. Is he all right? You don't need to say anything else. Thank you, Ana

units.title: Layer up! Thermal week at Camp Supply
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Brrr! The cold nights are here, and so is Thermal Week! Merino base layers, fleece-lined trousers and our famous double-cuff socks are all 25% off until Monday. Stay warm on site, at the allotment or on the school run. Remember: there's no such thing as bad weather, only the wrong socks!

units.title: Supply run times may move
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Morning. Sound Lines' freight desk has told us charter runs are being shuffled around the passenger sailings while the fog lasts. In practice, the supply boat may leave Gilliver up to two hours later than usual. The order itself isn't affected. If anyone is waiting at the landing, please make sure they're dressed for a long wait and not standing in the wet. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: A request from the client
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi. The client's community desk has asked, very politely, that crew don't post photographs of the island or the camp online while the work is going on. They didn't give a reason and I didn't ask. It's a reasonable thing for a private landowner to want. Could you mention it to everyone, without making a meeting of it? Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Local chatter
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi. You may see, if anyone has signal, that the local forums are having a lovely time guessing what the Holm is for. Hotels, data centres, a secret base. The Courier has even had the council say the paperwork is public. Please don't engage, and don't let it get into anyone's head. It's an ordinary clearance, just a big one. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: I should add, in fairness: I don't know what the client intends to do with the island either. Nobody here does, as far as I can tell, and I don't think it's our business. Our business is the trees, on time and safely. If anyone on the crew asks you, that's an honest answer you're welcome to give them. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Fuel prices
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi. The fuel berth at Gilliver is selling more diesel this week than it has all autumn, and the price has nudged up accordingly. It's still within budget. If you order fuel, it works out cheaper in full drums than part ones, because the berth charges a handling fee per container. Not urgent, just useful. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Radios in the cold
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi. A tip passed on from another site lead: handheld radio batteries lose charge quickly in damp cold, so keep spares inside the camper rather than in the tool store, and swap them at lunch. The radios are your link to each other in fog, so it's worth the bother. Spare batteries can go on the order. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Weekly check-in tomorrow
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi. Just a heads-up that I'll send the end-of-week check-in tomorrow, after Payroll have closed period one. There's nothing to prepare. If there's anything you've been meaning to raise and haven't wanted to bother me with, now is a good time; I'd rather hear about it on day seven than on day twenty. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Day six
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: End of day six. Thank you for the report. The Met Office still has the fog sitting on the Sound for a few more days, possibly until a front comes through at the weekend. The camp has been through worse, I'm sure. Do keep everyone near the camper after dark, and lights on where people walk. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: blue fabric: a saga
units.author: sam
units.text: the school needs blue fabric for the river in The Kingfisher and the King and I said I'd find some, so I've been to three charity shops and come home with a blue duvet cover with stars on it. the director says rivers don't have stars. Jamie says this one does. the river has stars now. I am a costume department. anyway. love, S x

units.title: your island is in the paper again
units.author: sam
units.text: the Courier says people online think the Holm is going to be a hotel or a data centre. Mum says a hotel, because 'rich people like views'. Jamie says a zoo. I said I'd ask you, but I know you can't say, or don't know, or both. if it's a hotel, can we have a discount? asking for Mum. love, S x

units.author: sam
units.text: also, Mum has a date now: the consultant wants to do the hip in about a fortnight. she's pretending she isn't nervous by reorganising the airing cupboard. I'll be with her. you don't need to do anything except stay warm and not fall over a tree. the dog sends a lick, which I declined to forward. love, S x

units.title: can't sleep, the foghorn
units.author: sam
units.text: you can hear the Carrow Point foghorn from our back bedroom tonight if the wind's the right way, which I didn't think was possible from Tollinby. probably it's the stillness. it sounds like a big animal yawning every thirty seconds. the dog has given up barking at it. I'm going to bed. sleep well out there. love, S x

units.title: What did the beaver say to the tree? (Nice gnawing you.)
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: I'm running out, chief. That's the bottom of the barrel. Somebody at the depot says the Holm crew are on a good rate. Not jealous. Mildly jealous. If they need someone who can tell a beech from a birch in the dark and do card tricks, I'm free in a month. Tell Ruth I said that, and watch her face. Actually don't.

units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Ignore the bit about the rate. Money's never the hard part on a job like that. The hard part is it's the same faces and the same dark every night for a month, and by week two somebody starts saying things at the fire they wouldn't say in daylight. Let them. Don't argue with it. Make tea. Anyway. Cribbage.

units.title: Card trick for the camp (you're welcome)
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Get someone to pick a card, any card, put it back, shuffle. Then say 'is this your card?' and hold up the wrong one. They'll say no. Then say 'oh well' and put the deck away. It's not a trick, it's a lesson in managing expectations. I learned it from Grieve head office. Night, chief.

units.title: Sorry again
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Hi, sorry to write again so soon. Nothing has happened, I just wanted to say the car is fixed and it was only a hose, so Tomas can stop worrying about that one. Please tell him I'm fine. I know he'll ask. And if he looks tired, you can tell him from me to go to bed, he listens to other people more than me. Thank you, Ana

units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: P.S. I realised I've never said thank you properly for letting me write. I know you're not a post office. He doesn't like asking for things, so if there's anything he needs out there, socks or anything, I could send it to the company and they could put it on the boat. Sorry. Ana

units.title: Soggy boots? Not on our watch!
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Wet weather means wet boots, and wet boots mean miserable mornings! Our boot dryer pack, three pairs of wax-cotton gaiters and a tin of our own-brand dubbin are bundled at a special price this week only. Plus: newsletter readers get a free pocket torch with any order over $40!

units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Three quick boot tips from our team! 1. Stuff wet boots with newspaper and change it every few hours. 2. Never dry leather right next to a stove; it cracks. 3. Leave them toes-up overnight so the water runs out, not in. Small habits, happy feet! See you next week at Camp Supply.

units.title: Re: pub sign (update nobody asked for)
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: The pub sign is now on the shed. My wife says it makes the garden look like a crime scene. I said every garden is a crime scene if you look closely at what the slugs do. She went inside. Anyway. Sleep well on your island, chief. Don't let the fog in the door.

units.title: Foggy joke (it's bad)
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Why did the fog get the job? Because it was mist-erious and nobody could see through it. That's what passes for wit on day three of a lay-by. The foreman has started doing crosswords out loud. If I go quiet, it's because I've walked into the reservoir out of boredom. I'm joking. I'm a strong swimmer.

units.title: Tollinby has gone grey
units.author: sam
units.text: the fog got here this morning, the market square looked like somebody had rubbed it out. Jamie walked to school holding the dog's lead and my sleeve like a little old man. the bus was forty minutes late and the driver gave everyone a mint. we don't know why. anyway, is it like this all day out there? love, S x

units.title: Gilliver contact
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi. If the supply boat is held at Gilliver in fog and you need to know what's happening, the harbour office is the quickest route. The harbourmaster is helpful and has our contact sheet. Please don't ring the skipper directly while he's under way, he's got enough on. My number stays the first call for anything else. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: A note from upstairs
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi. Passing on, word for word, a director's comment from this afternoon: 'Tell the Holm site lead the reports are good and we're not worried about fog.' That's the warmest thing I've heard him say about anything this year, so I thought you should have it. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Follow-up on the slipway: Sound FM have picked up the trespass report, so you may hear it mentioned. Nothing has changed for us. The boat is loading at the fuel berth, and the harbour office has been very good about it. If anyone on the crew has family ringing about the radio story, they can reassure them it's a harbour safety matter at Gilliver, not the Holm. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Following up on the generator hours, in case it's buried: fleet maintenance say if the counter is fogged up or hard to read, don't worry, they'll estimate from fuel use and send the filter kit on a boat next week anyway. One less thing. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Your renewal documents are ready to view
units.author: lyle_insurance
units.text: Dear policyholder, your renewal documents for policy LM-V-448120 are now ready to view in your online account. Please check that your details, including your usual address and the use of your vehicle, are correct. If your circumstances have changed, tell us before the renewal date. Peace of mind starts with the small print! Lyle Mutual Insurance.

units.author: sam
units.text: the director has come round to the stars. she says it's 'a river at night' now and the kingfisher has to cross it with a lantern. Jamie is beside himself because Second Reed gets to hold the lantern in act two. the limp is staying. I have been asked to make a lantern out of a jam jar. send ideas. love, S x

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: To be clear, since someone always asks: photos for the day report or for H&S are fine and still welcome, as those come to me and stay with Grieve. It's only social media and the like the client wants to avoid. Personal photos of each other at the fire are nobody's business but yours. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Landing and tides
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi. With neap tides this weekend the skipper says the landing beach will be easier than last week, as the water won't go as far out. Low water is around midday and just before midnight. He'd rather unload in the morning than at low tide, so if the boat seems early or late, that's the reason. Thanks, Ruth
